children: Japan’s currency has strengthened from above ¥160 to around ¥157 in two sessions. Friday’s US jobs report now determines whether the reversal has further to run.
Yen finally finds some momentum
The
pair fell a full 1% Thursday to under ¥157.00, its lowest level in about a month.
The yen gained around 0.9% Wednesday, transforming what initially looked like another failed defense of ¥160 into a considerably more serious two-session reversal.
Japan’s currency recently touched a 40-year low near ¥164 before
drove the pair as low as ¥155.20. Much of that recovery was subsequently surrendered.
The latest rally, by the looks of it, is being supported by changing rate expectations, not only government dollar sales.
There was early speculation that authorities had intervened again or conducted a “rate check” — when officials ask banks for live currency quotes, sometimes before entering the market.
Analysts increasingly attribute the move to hawkish Bank of Japan signals instead. This time, the yen may have brought its own fuel.
BOJ turns up the hawkishness
BOJ board member Hajime Takata said interest rates should rise nimbly in response to inflation rather than following a predictable twice-yearly schedule.
Governor Kazuo Ueda added that economic and price risks would be discussed at September’s meeting, leaving every policy gathering potentially live.
Markets now almost fully price a BOJ increase this month, with roughly 50 basis points of tightening expected by year-end.
A basis point equals one-hundredth of a percentage point. Japan’s two-year government yield climbed to 1.83% Wednesday, its highest since 1995.
Higher Japanese yields reduce the appeal of the carry trade — borrowing cheaply in yen to purchase higher-yielding foreign assets.
If the BOJ tightens faster, those positions become less profitable and may be unwound, forcing traders to buy back yen. The world’s favorite funding currency has started charging admission.
US payrolls control the other side

is expected to show approximately 56,000 new positions. Markets currently assign around a 60% chance to a September Federal Reserve rate increase. A weak report could reduce those odds, pull Treasury yields lower and extend the dollar-yen’s decline.
Strong payrolls and wage growth would support Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish stance, potentially sending the pair back toward ¥159 and ¥160.
The exchange rate remains a contest between two repricings: faster BOJ tightening on one side and another possible Fed increase on the other.
Levels to watch now: ¥157 is the immediate pivot, followed by support around ¥156 and the post-intervention low near ¥155.20.
Resistance sits at ¥159 and ¥160. A break below ¥157.50 would strengthen the bearish reversal; reclaiming ¥160 would suggest the yen’s comeback still requires official supervision.

title: USD/JPY: Yen Surges to One-Month High Under ¥157 on BOJ Rate-Hike Bets
